title: A Parade Worth Waiting For

source.outlet: New York Daily News（The Spokesman-Review 轉載）
source.headline: Historic postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade complicates plans for tourists and performers
source.author: Rebecca White, Emma Seiwell

article: For the first time since it began in 1924, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade did not march on Thanksgiving. A massive storm brought dangerous winds and {1|torrential} rain to New York, so organizers moved the event to Saturday. This year was meant to be special: to mark its {2|centennial}, Macy’s had planned to fly a record 100 balloons. Until now, the parade had been canceled only during World War II, when balloon materials were needed for the war effort. The sudden change created a {3|logistical} puzzle for thousands of visitors and performers who had built their trips around Thursday.

Some fans simply ran out of time. Alaina Roberts, 21, traveled from Boston after years of watching the parade on TV while her parents cooked dinner. Her train home left on Friday night, and changing the ticket cost too much, so she will miss it. “It’s super disappointing,” she said, although she admitted the parade could not have gone ahead in such weather. A tourist from Houston said many guests at his hotel had to fly home before Saturday. Another visitor, Zachary Garcia-Hochhaltar, agreed that safety came first: the volunteers who handle the balloons should not risk their lives in strong winds.

For marching bands, the delay came with a {4|hefty} price. Extra hotel nights, meals and transportation suddenly had to be paid for, and not every group could extend its stay. Elsewhere, former band members, families and donors across the country stepped in to {5|foot the bill}. Pearland High School in Texas raised $350,000 so that more than 500 students could stay. The Hawai’i All-State Marching Band faced costs of over $700,000 and had raised more than $500,000, leaving a painful {6|shortfall}. {7|Undeterred}, its leaders announced that the band would remain in New York and perform anyway.

Not everyone sees the delay as a loss. Some even hope for a small {8|windfall}: a liquor store worker along the route expects a jump in sales on Saturday instead of Thanksgiving Day. Macy’s says it is saddened but optimistic. Will Coss, who heads Macy’s Studios, said his team had spent more than two years on the parade and promised the biggest and best one in its history. The weather service forecast a partly sunny Saturday with much calmer winds, giving the giant balloons a far better chance to fly.
article_zh: 梅西百貨感恩節大遊行自 1924 年開辦以來，第一次沒有在感恩節當天登場。一場強烈暴風雨為紐約帶來危險的強風和傾盆大雨，主辦單位因此把活動延到週六。今年原本意義非凡：為了紀念一百週年，梅西百貨計畫施放破紀錄的 100 顆氣球。在此之前，這場遊行只在二戰期間停辦過，因為當時製作氣球的材料必須優先供應戰爭所需。這次突如其來的改期，讓數千名把行程排在週四的遊客和表演者，面臨一場調度安排上的難題。

有些粉絲就是時間不夠。21 歲的艾蕾娜・羅伯茲從波士頓專程前來，她多年來都是一邊看電視轉播遊行，一邊等爸媽煮晚餐。她回程的火車在週五晚上，改票太貴，所以她只能錯過遊行。「真的超級失望。」她說，不過她也承認，在那樣的天氣下遊行根本不可能照常舉行。一位來自休士頓的遊客說，他住的飯店裡有很多為了遊行而來的客人，都得在週六前搭機回家。另一位遊客札卡里・賈西亞－霍查爾塔也認為安全第一：負責操控氣球的志工不該冒著強風拿生命開玩笑。
對樂儀隊來說，延期代價不小。多住幾晚飯店、餐費和交通費突然都得有人支付，而且並不是每個團體都能延長停留。另一方面，全美各地的樂隊校友、家長和捐款人紛紛出手買單。德州的皮爾蘭高中募到 35 萬美元，讓 500 多名學生得以留下。夏威夷全州聯合樂隊則面臨超過 70 萬美元的開銷，雖已募得 50 多萬美元，仍留下令人頭痛的資金缺口。但樂隊領導層並未退縮，宣布全隊將留在紐約，照樣上場表演。
並不是每個人都把延期當成損失。有些人甚至期待一筆小小的意外之財：遊行路線旁一家酒行的店員預期，週六的業績會比原本感恩節當天還要好。梅西百貨表示雖然遺憾，但仍保持樂觀。梅西百貨工作室負責人威爾・考斯說，團隊花了兩年多籌備這場遊行，並承諾這會是史上規模最大、最精采的一次。氣象局預報週六局部晴朗、風勢平穩許多，讓巨型氣球順利升空的機會大增。
summary_zh: 原定感恩節舉行、適逢第 100 屆的梅西百貨感恩節大遊行，因強烈暴風雨帶來強風豪雨，史上第一次延期到週六。改期打亂了許多遊客的行程，有人因改票太貴只能錯過；各地樂儀隊也得臨時籌措多出來的住宿和交通費，夏威夷樂隊即使資金仍有缺口，仍決定留下表演。梅西百貨則承諾會端出史上最盛大的一屆遊行。
